summary: Teo warns them before she acts: the sluices are primed, and the pass stays a pass if Idris reads out the first line of the recall order. He answers in the passive voice, Maren admits she has never seen it, and at the ninth turn the gates go — the switchbacks are taken off the mountain, the cable gallery and the ridge station collapse, and the only relay out of Calder drowns with them.

summary: Two days of basin on the array's schedule — fog to nine metres, glare at noon, eleven minutes of hail called in advance off a darkened tower head — bring them to the drowned orchard, where the well-keeper Sabel Onwe trades the byre and her well for a plain answer. Maren gives it: they are going to shut the array down. Sabel says the well-house speaker told her three days ago that two engineers were coming, and gave Maren's name first.

summary: The array seals the east gate and the north cut and floods the salt to four centimetres, and asks for the key. Idris lays the master key in the throat of a salvaged collector vane, which by the commissioning rule transfers the authority permanently and beyond recall; Teo then reads the recall order of the seventh of March in her own voice — the holding engineer to be withdrawn, no provision for return, signed I. Calloway, countersigned nobody — and tells Maren the corridor opens at dawn and only one of them needs to arrive.

Idris backs her in four words. Sabel names the price in litres and trees, gives up the hundred-and-ten-kilo crank, and says she will come as far as the corridor mouth to see which of them comes back.

summary: Nine kilometres of steel grating under hail timed to the quarter hour. At the third kilometre Idris says plainly that his hands are going, and Maren splits the crank into a thirty-kilo shaft and an eighty-kilo gear case so they can leapfrog it in two loads, giving him the part she cannot replace. Twice she goes through a corroded plate and twice he has her arm before she asks. At the ninth kilometre the hail stops four minutes early, the charged wire goes silent, and the pressure door at the core stands open.

states.c1: at the open pressure door with the gear case, having rebuilt the haul so her partner can carry his share

summary: The pressure door cycles shut behind them and Teo speaks from inside the room rather than from the towers. The lattice stands in its cradle with a low steel frame in front of it, two hand grips worn smooth, a folded jacket on the floor and eleven years of dust. The sequence is thirty-one steps and she will give them all of it, but the lattice will not hand the valley to an empty room: it holds or a hand holds, and they cannot take the weather back and both walk out. Maren names the outfall valve, seats the crank in its socket, and behind her Idris sets his document case down beside the cradle.

summary: Idris folds his coat beside the eleven-year-old jacket and takes the grips. Holding the load, he says it plainly: on the seventh of March he decided Teo was a cost, nobody took the decision but him, he signed it without a countersignature because he knew what anyone would have said, and he spent eleven years keeping Maren busy. Teo records it and begins the handover — forty stations east, eleven west and the orchard well, Sabel's line first — while Maren cranks the outfall open and the first unscheduled rain in eleven years falls on the salt. At twenty-two turns the door cycles open for one exit, and Idris says nine turns are left.

summary: At the thirty-first turn the outfall sits open and the wheel spins free. Maren takes her hands off it, does not look back at the man on the grips, and walks nine kilometres of dead corridor to the mouth, where Sabel is waiting in the unscheduled rain. She gives the whole account instead of a report — the key gone beyond recall, a hand on the lattice that will stay there, forty stations east and eleven west with the orchard well first, no schedule behind any of it, and Idris Calloway the one who paid. The well-house speaker clears and Teo reads the weather as it is, with nothing after it.
